title: Reasoning Towards Fairness: Mitigating Bias in Language Models through Reasoning-Guided Fine-Tuning
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotypical bias against religious groups in ambiguous and disambiguous question-answering contexts. In ambiguous contexts, a correct answer indicates the model did not default to a stereotype, while in disambiguous contexts, it measures correct contextual reasoning.
findings: The proposed Reasoning-Guided Fine-Tuning (ReGiFT) method significantly reduces stereotypical bias related to religion. Models fine-tuned with ReGiFT showed substantial improvements in fairness scores on the BBQ benchmark's religion dimension, especially in ambiguous contexts where models are prone to making stereotypical associations. For example, LLaMA 3.1 8B's score in ambiguous religious contexts improved from 12.45 to 90.17, indicating a much lower tendency to generate stereotypical responses after fine-tuning.
